framework: WIDA English Language Development Standards Framework, 2020 Edition
alignmentNotes: Local domain and Key Language Use tags describe instructional focus; a tag alone is not a full Language Expectation crosswalk.
A verified WIDA Language Expectation crosswalk records grade cluster, ELD Standard, Key Language Use, communication mode and expectation.
Grades 3-5 is a local content band spanning WIDA grade clusters 2-3 and 4-5. Local A/B/C labels are support choices, not WIDA proficiency levels.

notOfficial: This blueprint describes how this lab's classroom practice is organized. It is not an official WIDA or ACCESS test blueprint, and nothing in the lab produces a WIDA score, proficiency level or placement. For official sample items use WIDA's ACCESS practice page.

standards.name: Language for Social and Instructional purposes

keyLanguageUses.definition: Tell stories and recount experiences or events in sequence.
Describe, define and present factual information about a topic.
Account for how things work or why things happen.
Make a claim and support it with reasons and evidence.

dimensions.definition: Organization, cohesion and density of a whole spoken or written text.
Grammatical complexity and control within and across sentences.
Precision and appropriateness of vocabulary and phrases.

purposes.label: Instructional practice
purposes.description: Supports are open (frames, word bank, model, transcript, hints). Feedback comes while learning. Evidence is recorded as supported.
features: Studios at 'frames and words' or 'word bank'

purposes.label: Independent practice (ACCESS-style)
purposes.description: No supports are open during the attempt. Feedback arrives after the learner submits. Evidence is recorded as independent and is never mixed with supported attempts.

purposes.label: Official ACCESS
purposes.description: Only WIDA and your state administer ACCESS. The lab never presents its results as ACCESS scores. Speaking and Writing on the official test are scored by trained raters with WIDA's current rubrics.

domains.officialFormat: Selected response, machine-scored on ACCESS Online.
domains.labFormat: Mission audio with 2–4 speakers (read by the device voice), a transcript alternative that is recorded as a support, questions tagged by skill with named distractor types, and evidence collection.

domains.officialFormat: Selected response, machine-scored on ACCESS Online.
domains.labFormat: Mission passages with charts and tables, core and stretch questions (stretch only after independent success), inference and cross-source synthesis, evidence selection.

domains.officialFormat: Recorded responses to prompts, scored by trained raters.
domains.labFormat: Recorded spoken production: retell, describe, compare, explain, argue, discuss. Plan, rehearse, record, listen back, review, re-record. Language Coach reads the learner's typed transcript; time and pauses are measured on the device.

domains.officialFormat: Extended written responses, scored by trained raters.
domains.labFormat: Source-based writing from guided to independent: paragraph, claim-evidence-reasoning, summary, report, narrative, letter, essay. Draft history, targeted feedback, revision, evidence notebook, portfolio.

coverageMethod: See the generated activity-level alignment inventory in alignment-index.json. Counts distinguish author-entered local tags from verified Language Expectation crosswalks; blank or unreviewed metadata is reported as a gap.

rules.text: No two options in an item may be identical.
The key points at an option that exists.
No answer position may hold more than half of a pool's keys.
The correct option should not be conspicuously the longest in most items.
Review distractors that can be rejected by an absolute word rather than by evidence or reasoning; accurate time expressions such as every summer are not automatically a defect.
Use Flesch–Kincaid only as a screening signal. Short passages, dialogue, names, numbers and science or math notation can distort the estimate; an educator reviews readability in context.
Mission questions tag every wrong option with the reading mistake it represents so feedback can be specific.
